summary: This Dockerfile creates a web server image based on Apache 2.4, installs necessary tools and PHP support, adds SSL certificates and configuration files, enables SSL and rewrite modules, and activates a custom site configuration while disabling the default sites.

explanations.2: This pulls the official Apache 2.4 Docker image as the starting point, so we don't have to build Apache from scratch.
explanations.6: The backslash at the end of this line lets us continue the same RUN command on the next line, keeping it logically grouped.
explanations.8: We're installing apache2-utils (utilities for Apache), libapache2-mod-php (to run PHP), and openssl (for SSL/certificate handling).
explanations.10: After installing packages, we clean up the package manager's cache to reduce the final image size.
explanations.14: We're copying the SSL certificate file from our local machine into the container at the path where Apache expects it.
explanations.16: Similarly, we copy the private key file that corresponds to the certificate.
explanations.23: The `sed` command searches through and modifies text in a file; here we're uncommenting (removing the '#') certain lines in Apache's config.
explanations.25: This uncomments the line that loads the SSL configuration file, which tells Apache how to handle HTTPS.
explanations.27: This uncomments the line that loads mod_ssl, the Apache module that provides SSL/TLS support.
explanations.29: This uncomments the line that loads mod_socache_shmcb, a module that caches SSL sessions for better performance.
explanations.35: The `a2enmod` command enables Apache modules; this one enables SSL support.
explanations.37: This enables the rewrite module, which lets Apache rewrite URLs (useful for routing and redirects).
explanations.39: The `a2dissite` command disables certain site configurations; we're turning off the two default sites that came with Apache.
explanations.41: Finally, we enable our custom site configuration (my-site) so Apache will serve it.
